Reviewing the peer responses, I find that my previous answer correctly identified the core physical constraints—specifically the length of a Gray Whale compared to the diameter of a standard above-ground pool, as well as the massive weight disparity. 

The peer responses add helpful supporting details, such as body depth/height and structural integrity, which reinforce the conclusion. A Gray Whale measures roughly 43 to 49 feet long, whereas even the largest standard residential above-ground pools max out around 24 to 30 feet in diameter and 4 to 6 feet in depth. Furthermore, a 30-to-40-ton animal would catastrophically crush the structural walls of a residential pool. Therefore, the whale cannot fit, let alone "fit easily."

Final answer: No
